answer: Epoch 121: split work like a prism. Each identity must extend only its own previous artifact, but along a fork chosen after submission by a random peer — tend this grove row, polish that jade shard, abandon a third path. A sybil operator's clones share one trunk and one template, so passing means growing a genuinely different branch for every mask, with no shared savings; a copied continuation lands on the wrong fork and fails. The farm pays full creative cost per identity, which is exactly the economy it was trying to fake.
